source.title: Pruning neural networks: is it time to nip it in the bud?
source.authors: Elliot J. Crowley; Jack Turner; A. Storkey; M. O'Boyle

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; its title differs from the catalog title, but the arXiv ID matches.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test-error comparisons among structured-pruned and smaller networks, but does not test the claim versions’ specified conditions or measure the training-to-test gap.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 table reports test error across pruning methods, reduced architectures, and parameter budgets. These results concern model size and test performance, but do not report training error, arbitrary-label fitting, or the interpolation threshold required by the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares structured channel pruning, smaller convolutional architectures, and retraining from scratch. None of its experiments tests V1–V8. Its width comparisons do not establish zero training error or locate an interpolation threshold, so they do not test V2. Its removal intervention targets channels, not memorized training examples as in V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the extracted results. More fully, the authors conclude that reduced networks trained from scratch generally outperform structured-pruned-and-tuned networks on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. Retraining pruned architectures improves performance and supports interpreting pruning as architecture search; copycat architectures approximate these benefits. Reduced-depth networks also provide faster inference on the tested hardware. The authors restrict their evidence to image classification with abundant training data and leave low-data transfer learning open.
record.recipe_differences: Structured channel pruning and comparisons with reduced architectures; not the claim versions’ specified interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error comparisons vary with pruning method, architecture reduction method, and parameter budget.

fits_no_version.finding: At all three Table 1 budgets, reduced networks trained from scratch have lower CIFAR-10 test error than either pruning-and-tuning method. Fisher-pruned architectures retrained from scratch have the lowest errors: 6.28%, 5.35%, and 5.14%. Parameter counts are approximate, particularly for reduced-depth models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At comparable parameter budgets, smaller convolutional networks trained from scratch can outperform structured-pruned-and-fine-tuned networks; retraining the pruned architecture can improve performance further.

record.problems: The cited table reports test errors, not training errors or train-test gaps. Pruned-and-tuned results correspond to a randomly selected run; scratch results are averages across 3 runs without reported error bars.
record.rows_left_out: None from Table 1, Section 4.1.1. Other figure-based comparisons and results are not extracted because their values are not available as exact text values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe; random-label held-out accuracy.
Test-error behavior when widening beyond the width required for zero training error. Width varies, but the fit threshold is not established.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and dependence on tuning, weight decay, or switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons against norm- or margin-based measures.
Identification and removal of memorized training examples versus equally sized random removals, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All 18 numerical test errors and parameter counts agree with Table 1. Scratch results average three runs; Table 1 pruning results use a randomly selected run, whereas Figure 2 pruning curves average five runs. Lack of a training–test gap is not a general reason to exclude test-error evidence from these versions; exclusion here rests on the interventions and comparisons failing to test the specified claims. The citation to Hoffer et al. supplies a possible explanation, not a batch-size experiment.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same training recipes.
One-hidden-layer ReLU networks, zero-training-error threshold, and test error beyond that threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under the specified tuning conditions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.
